from_quote: That which empowers the new Congress to make all laws that may be necessary and proper for carrying into execution any of their powers
rationale: The paragraph names, among "the following clause[s]," the one empowering Congress to make all laws necessary and proper for executing its powers, closely echoing Article I, Section 8, Clause 18.
to_quote: To make all Laws which shall be necessary and proper for carrying into Execution

from_quote: that which ordains that their acts shall be the supreme law of the land, anything in the laws or constitution of any State to the contrary notwithstanding
rationale: The paragraph names the clause making the acts of Congress the supreme law of the land notwithstanding State constitutions or laws, paraphrasing the supremacy clause of Article VI.
to_quote: shall be the supreme Law of the Land

from_quote: that which gives Congress the absolute control over the time and mode of its appointment and election
rationale: The paragraph names the clause giving Congress control over the time and manner of electing its members, which is Article I, Section 4, Clause 1.

from_quote: that which authorizes them to keep on foot at all times a standing army
rationale: The paragraph names the clause authorizing Congress to keep an army, which is the power to raise and support armies in Article I, Section 8, Clause 12.
